newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: U.S. seeks non-political EU probe on Boeing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. seeks non-political EU probe on Boeing.

text.p: The United States said on Wednesday that it was seeking assurances from the European Union that a European probe into Boeing's planned merger with McDonnell Douglas would not be political.

U.S. trade representative Charlene Barshefsky told reporters that the U.S. wanted "assurances that the inquiry must be conducted on competition policy principles and not on extraneous political principles."

U.S. officials said that the planned $14 billion merger between the two U.S. airplane manufacturers, one of the most contentious issues in today's trans-Atlantic relations, had not come up directly at a twice-yearly U.S.-EU summit in The Hague.
The European Commission, the EU's antitrust watchdog, has expressed grave concerns about the effect on competition of the deal, which also comes under scrutiny from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission.

Barshefsky noted differences between the way in which Europe and the United States conduct such competition probes, saying that Washington could not overrule a U.S. Federal Trade Commission decision but that the European Commission can have the final say over an advisers' report -- hence U.S. fears that Europe could be swayed by political motives.

Brussels said last week that the aerospace mega-merger would leave the world market with only two major commercial aircraft manufacturers -- Boeing and Europe's Airbus Industrie -- a consortium of France's Aerospatiale, British Aerospace, Germany's DASA and Spain's Construcciones Aeronautiocas.
